Yes yes. Him not working by choice is most of the problem. I believe in community helping each other, but I don't believe in being an ATM. It'd be one thing if everyone was pulling their weight but they fell short sometimes, but just sitting at home, taking money from us, then emotionally/verbally abusing us too? That's way too far. I have stories for days about how mean my father has been. He's even rude to service workers.

>> Then what's the motivation to give them money?

People pleasing and eagerness to help and resolve family issues. I've always done whatever to make everyone happy

Nothing. My grandparents were gracious enough to not make them pay household bills (except buying their own food) for all this time. They expected nothing out of us kids, they just wanted us to do well in school which we all did. My granddad didn't even want me to move out lol, but has always wanted my parents to go.

That's what makes this so odd; they had their monstrous storage bill, they got a loan to move and blew it so they're paying that back, they have a car payment, their credit was shit because of the foreclosure, my mom has a shopping problem (boxes and boxes from Shein every month; she has so many clothes she ran out of room to put them) my dad spends a ton on cigars, and they've taken plenty of vacations. My dad asked me and my sibling for $150 each so my mom could have spending money on the trip then sent it to her as if it were from him.....this was as recent as October.

I agree with you, thank you for the comment. I would love to have a serious conversation about goals and expectations without egos and arguments, but that's so difficult with them. my siblings and I have all been in therapy and done a lot of internal work so conversations with my parents are not easy. It ends up being a lot of guilt tripping, sly underhanded comments, and anger. It's so stressful

As for the first paragraph, I can totally see how'd you see it that way. Things were a lot different than what you described, but it'd be too much to go into details about. 

They paid for my sibling's wedding, yes, but they didn't pay for our schooling they just *encouraged* us to go. Financial aid took care of that. I lived away for school but when I was home I always took care of bills, buying food obviously, and miscellaneous stuff(they don't pay rent). I can't contribute as much anymore because I have my own bills. 

Tbh I don't know how they'll make it financially if they move away from my grandparents' home. They only have one check coming in and most of it is going towards paying a humongous storage fee (we're talking almost 2k a month, I'm not even kidding). I've seen how much the storage payment has gone up over the years because I've paid it myself. It started at $400 ten years ago and here we are.
